acceptance_criteria: Sink success returns channel=sink and status=captured, never a dispatcher-owned durability or transport-acceptance status.
Callers that require dispatcher ownership reject captured, accepted-unconfirmed, rejected, failed, and no-channel outcomes without advancing lifecycle state.
A normal application process with the sink key present fails closed before message processing with only the key name and a bounded reason code.
An explicitly authorized verifier can capture alerts and clears, cannot enqueue or invoke a live helper, and advertises capture mode through metadata-only startup, health, and receipt fields.
Verifier capture authority and the scoped live-producer authority from #2391 are mutually exclusive, locally attestable, and unavailable through ambient default state.
Managed wrapper, systemd, deployment-owned launchd, and container fixtures prove the sink cannot be inherited accidentally.
Capture failure never falls through to the durable outbox or legacy helper and returns a distinct rejected or failed result.
Durability quarantine, incident marker, transport latch, scheduler latch, fleet recovery, and restart tests cover captured separately from dispatcher-owned durability.
The alert outcome vocabulary integrates with #2447 without making its cross-contract PR own this startup and route-authority boundary.
All tests, logs, health fields, and public artifacts use bounded enums and reserved synthetic identities without path values, destinations, credentials, or private topology.

evidence_summary: Exact pinned blobs prove that any non-empty ambient WHATSOUP_ALERT_SINK enters capture before the durable outbox and legacy helper, appends one local record, and returns ok=true, channel=sink, status=durably_queued. observeAlertEmission then reduces that result to true. A write-free deterministic source canary verified the contract, found no sink validation in the managed wrapper, systemd unit, container entrypoint, bootstrap, or health projection, and checked six representative durability, incident-marker, transport-latch, scheduler-latch, and recovery-clear transitions that advance on the checked boolean. The focused sink test explicitly expects no outbox file, no helper spawn, and true. Exact pagination across all 38 open pull requests and 1,327 changed-file records found no owner or issue reference. Draft PR #2495 modifies the emitter for a separate protocol proposal but preserves the sink durably_queued result and lacks capture authority or startup exclusion. falsifier_or_remaining_gap: A distinct captured outcome rejected by durability-requiring callers, explicit verifier-scoped authority, and fail-closed production startup plus metadata-only health attestation would falsify the source defect. This audit did not set the sink, append a capture file, run suites that create temporary directories, inspect any live service environment, or claim that a deployed process currently has the key; runtime and deployment incidence remain unmeasured.
impact: A production process that inherits the sink can record alert and clear obligations as satisfied while creating no dispatcher-owned event and making no operator-facing transport attempt. Lifecycle latches can suppress retries, quarantine and recovery gates can advance, and incident markers can be persisted or deleted on local capture alone.
